label: Inside the edit
blurb: Seven separate skills that all happen in one application, which is why the application looks so intimidating.

nodes.label: Assembly cut
nodes.blurb: Everything usable in order, far too long. You cannot judge structure until the whole thing exists badly.

nodes.label: Pacing
nodes.blurb: Cutting the parts you enjoyed making. The single largest difference between a build log and a video.

nodes.label: B-roll
nodes.blurb: Cutaways that cover a jump and show the detail. Shot after the edit exists, once you know what is missing.

nodes.label: Sound mix
nodes.blurb: Levels, music under voice, and room tone under silence. Viewers forgive a soft picture and leave over bad sound.

nodes.label: Titles
nodes.blurb: Names, labels and the number that tells somebody which part they are on. Small, and usually the last thing done.

nodes.label: Captions
nodes.blurb: Burned in or as a track. Half of all viewing is muted, and captions are how a deaf viewer gets in at all.

nodes.label: Proxies
nodes.blurb: Editing against small copies so the timeline scrubs, then relinking to the originals to export. A workflow, not a setting.

edges.note: You only know which cutaway you need once the cut is tight enough to show the gap.
